title: Reference images on boxes: a box names the reference picture it takes its subject from (FLUX.3 Klein + MOSS-Image)
description: Fabio 2026-10-27 (from MPI-1309): let each layout box name ONE reference picture, so 'the character from picture 2 goes in this box' is said to the model in its own trained format, not in prose. For FLUX.3 Klein AND MOSS-Image. Why: several character sheets in one generation make FLUX.3 draw extra copies (5 sheets -> 6-8 robots) and mix parts; wording, Qwen-Image 2.1 and cropping are all ruled out (MPI-1309 validation.md). NEVER crop a sheet, users make their own sheets (gallery combine), any layout. FLUX.3 findings (research session, read-only, 2026-10-27): FLUX.3 edit is t2i with references (comfy_workflows/flux3_t2i.json node 699 starts blank; MpiFlux3References). BFL's i2i_bbox layout rows are {id, from: 'ref_image_N', src_bbox, tgt_bbox, desc} and the text cites '<cup_1> from <ref_image_1>' (copy in tasks/MPI-1181/research/bfl_pup_system_prompts.json); src_bbox can be the whole sheet [0,0,1000,1000]. Today layoutRows (js/data/layoutBoxes.js:41-56) writes only {id,bbox,desc}; withLayoutBoxes (js/data/generationControls.js:368-386) adds a 'keep everything else the same' line to every boxed edit, wrong when Custom size is on (a new composition). The node already renumbers ref tags past empty slots (flux3.py:38). Untested: BFL's blog and pup model card list boxes and refs separately. MOSS-Image: boxes exist on t2i only (docs/agent/models/moss-image.md 'Boxes'), no reference input today - first find whether MOSS can take a reference at all. Plan: (1) bench FLUX.3 by hand-written prompt on 2-3 sheets with Custom size on, ref rows vs today's rows, count characters; (2) research MOSS; (3) only then: an optional picture number per box, the ref row, drop the keep line under Custom size, a picture picker per box row in the panel. Also noticed: in Fabio's hand tests the clean results used the first reference's own size; custom 16:9 broke more - bench the size too. Later: Storyboard (MPI-1309) uses this to place each pictured character in its own box.
